page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sgn7i-vws-m4s.2xlarge is a virtual workstation and compute-optimized instance equipped with fractional GPU acceleration. Built on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock of 2.9 GHz. The instance allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with two threads per core, backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI support, AES, and SHA-NI.

Hardware memory configuration stands at 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Graphical and parallel compute processing is delivered via a shared slice of an NVIDIA A10 GPU, specifically a 0.1667 partition providing 4 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance does not include local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements position the general CPU performance squarely in the median percentile across workloads. The Intel Xeon platform achieved 1489.0 in Geekbench single-core, 7000.0 in multi-core, and a PassMark CPU score of 15297.69. Multi-core stress-ng reached 13123.11, while caching and decompression metrics showed single-threaded gzip compression at 27.54 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 38.4 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput logged 13.45 GB/sec alongside 13.18 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

The constrained fractional GPU and modest 4 GB VRAM influence its AI and accelerator capabilities. While lightweight language model tasks perform moderately well—generating 165.78 tokens per second on a small 135M model—medium 7B parameter inference degrades sharply to 7.03 tokens per second, with large 70B models unsupported. Memory benchmarks also registered in the lower quartile, with a PassMark memory score of 1621.48.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the fractional allocation of an enterprise NVIDIA A10 accelerator avoids the expense of renting a dedicated full GPU when baseline graphics or small-model inference is required. The lack of bundled local disks requires factoring in external storage costs. This configuration is best matched with lightweight visual workstation environments, basic 3D and ray tracing tasks, entry-level AI inference, and compute workloads requiring vector acceleration.
